arxiv-2107-02123.title: Stellarator coil design using cubic splines for improved access on the outboard side
arxiv-2107-02123.creator: Nicola Lonigro, Caoxiang Zhu
arxiv-2107-02123.description: Abstract In recent years many efforts have been undertaken to simplify coil designs for stellarators due to the difficulties in fabricating non-planar coils. The FOCUS code removes the need for a winding surface and represents the coils as arbitrary curves in 3D.

arxiv-2208-07308.title: Pose Forecasting in Industrial Human-Robot Collaboration
arxiv-2208-07308.creator: Alessio Sampieri, Guido Maria D’Amely di Melendugno, Andrea Avogaro, Federico Cunico, Francesco Setti, Geri Skenderi, Marco Cristani, Fabio Galasso
arxiv-2208-07308.description: Abstract Pushing back the frontiers of collaborative robots in industrial environments, we propose a new Separable-Sparse Graph Convolutional Network (SeS-GCN) for pose forecasting. For the first time, SeS-GCN bottlenecks the interaction of the spatial, temporal and channel-wise dimensions in GCNs, and it learns sparse adjacency matrices by a teacher-student framework. Compared to the state-of-the-art, it only uses 1.

arxiv-2208-11970.title: Understanding Diffusion Models: A Unified Perspective
arxiv-2208-11970.creator: Calvin Luo
arxiv-2208-11970.description: Abstract Contents Introduction: Generative Models Given observed samples {\bm{x}} from a distribution of interest, the goal of a generative model is to learn to model its true data distribution p({\bm{x}}) . Once learned, we can generate new samples from our approximate model at will.

arxiv-2212-00744.title: Improving astroBERT using Semantic Textual Similarity
arxiv-2212-00744.creator: Felix Grezes, Thomas Allen, Sergi Blanco-Cuaresma, Alberto Accomazzi, Michael J. Kurtz, Golnaz Shapurian, Edwin Henneken, Carolyn S. Grant, Donna M. Thompson, Timothy W. Hostetler, Matthew R. Templeton, Kelly E. Lockhart, Shinyi Chen, Jennifer Koch, Taylor Jacovich, Pavlos Protopapas
arxiv-2212-00744.description: Abstract The NASA Astrophysics Data System (ADS) is an essential tool for researchers that allows them to explore the astronomy and astrophysics scientific literature, but it has yet to exploit recent advances in natural language processing. At ADASS 2021, we introduced astroBERT, a machine learning language model tailored to the text used in astronomy papers in ADS.

arxiv-2301-05948.title: tasksource: A Dataset Harmonization Framework for Streamlined NLP Multi-Task Learning and Evaluation
arxiv-2301-05948.creator: Damien Sileo
arxiv-2301-05948.description: Abstract The HuggingFace Datasets Hub hosts thousands of datasets, offering exciting opportunities for language model training and evaluation. However, datasets for a specific task type often have different schemas, making harmonization challenging 1 1 1 https://xkcd.com/927/ . Multi-task training or evaluation necessitates manual work to fit data into task templates.

arxiv-2511-09589.title: Convergence analysis of a third order semi-implicit projection method for Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert equation
arxiv-2511-09589.creator: Changjian Xie, Cheng Wang
arxiv-2511-09589.description: Abstract . The convergence analysis of a third-order scheme for the highly nonlinear Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert equation with a non-convex constraint is considered. In this paper, we first present a fully discrete semi-implicit method for solving the Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert equation based on the third-order backward differentiation formula and the one-sided extrapolation (using previous time-step numerical values).

arxiv-2601-10019.title: Time Aggregation Features for XGBoost Models
arxiv-2601-10019.creator: Mykola Pinchuk, PhD
arxiv-2601-10019.description: Abstract This paper studies time aggregation features for XGBoost models in click-through rate prediction. The setting is the Avazu click-through rate prediction dataset with strict out-of-time splits and a no-lookahead feature constraint. Features for hour H H use only impressions from hours strictly before H H .

arxiv-2602-07823.title: Semi-device-independent certification of high-dimensional quantum channels
arxiv-2602-07823.creator: Mengyan Li, Yanning Jia, Fenzhuo Guo, Haifeng Dong, Sujuan Qin, Fei Gao
arxiv-2602-07823.description: Abstract Certifying high-dimensional quantum channels is essential for ensuring the reliability of quantum communication protocols. Existing certification schemes often rely on fully trusted internal devices, which is difficult to achieve in realistic scenarios. Here, we propose a semi-device-independent framework for certifying channel properties directly from observed statistics, assuming only that the system dimension is known.

arxiv-2602-15341.title: Testing Monotonicity of Real-Valued Functions on DAGs
arxiv-2602-15341.creator: Yuichi Yoshida
arxiv-2602-15341.description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by Yuichi Yoshida. We study monotonicity testing of real-valued functions on directed acyclic graphs (DAGs) with n n vertices. For every constant δ > 0 \delta>0 , we prove a Ω ⁡ ( n 1 / 2 − δ / ε ) \Omega(n^{1/2-\delta}/\sqrt{\varepsilon}) lower bound against non-adaptive two-sided testers on DAGs, nearly matching the classical O ⁡ ( n / ε ) O(\sqrt{n/\varepsilon}) -query upper bound.

plos-pone-0004291.title: Loss of Magel2 , a Candidate Gene for Features of Prader-Willi Syndrome, Impairs Reproductive Function in Mice
plos-pone-0004291.creator: Rebecca E. Mercer, Rachel Wevrick
plos-pone-0004291.description: PLOS ONE research article. MAGEL2 is one of several genes typically inactivated in the developmental obesity disorder Prader-Willi syndrome (PWS). The physiological consequences of loss of MAGEL2 , but without the concurrent loss of other PWS genes, are not well understood. Gene-targeted mutation of Magel2

pmc-10604301.title: Biological Characterization of Cleome felina L.f. Extracts for Phytochemical, Antimicrobial, and Hepatoprotective Activities in Wister Albino Rats
pmc-10604301.creator: Heena Yaqub Shaikh, Shaik Kalimulla Niazi, Asmatanzeem Bepari, Mary Anne Wong Cordero, Shazima Sheereen, Syed Arif Hussain, Muthuraj Rudrappa, Shashiraj Kariyellappa Nagaraja, Shekappa Ningappa Agadi
pmc-10604301.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). The present study aims to explore the phytochemical constitution and biological activities of Cleome felina L.f. felina (leaves, stem, and root) extracts (acetone, methanol, and water) were qualitatively assessed for phytochemical presence. Methanolic leaves extract revealed more positive phyto-compounds among all the extracts; further, methanolic leaves extract was evaluated for FTIR, EDX, GCMS, antimicrobial assay, acute toxicity, and paracetamol-induced hepatoprotective activity in Wister albino rats. FTIR and EDX analysis unveiled important functional groups and elements in the leaves.

pmc-10652719.title: Imidazolium-Based Ionic Liquid-Assisted Silver Nanoparticles and Their Antibacterial Activity: Experimental and Density Functional Theory Studies
pmc-10652719.creator: Elham Avirdi, Hugues Kamdem Paumo, Boniface Pone Kamdem, Madhur Babu Singh, Kamlesh Kumari, Lebogang Katata-Seru, Indra Bahadur
pmc-10652719.description: The exclusive properties of ionic liquids (ILs) offer various opportunities to develop advanced materials with appreciable therapeutic applications. Imidazolium-based ILs have been frequently used as reaction media and stabilizers for the development and surface functionalization of noble metal nanoparticles (NPs).

pmc-11290095.title: Escape room design in training crew resource management in acute care: a scoping review
pmc-11290095.creator: Gerald J Jaspers, Simone Borsci, Johannes G van der Hoeven, Wietske Kuijer-Siebelink, Joris Lemson
pmc-11290095.description: BackgroundEffective teamwork is crucial to providing safe and high-quality patient care, especially in acute care. Crew Resource Management (CRM) principles are often used for training teamwork in these situations, with escape rooms forming a promising new tool. However, little is known about escape room design characteristics and their effect on learning outcomes.

pmc-12598170.title: “B”-Stitches: A Technique for Repair of Traumatic Horizontal or Oblique Meniscal Tear
pmc-12598170.creator: Winyou Ratanachai, Charoen Chotigavanich
pmc-12598170.description: A horizontal tear of the meniscus is one of the most common meniscal tear patterns. This article presents a technique for horizontal meniscal repair called the B-stitch technique, including the logic behind its design. The B-stitch technique is a repair method that provides a reproducible and safe repair construct.

pmc-12654456.title: Altered Pulmonary Glucose Transport Is Restored by Metformin Treatment in an Obese Type 2 Diabetic Animal Model
pmc-12654456.creator: Allison Campolo, Zahra Maria, Véronique A. Lacombe
pmc-12654456.description: Background/Objectives: Obesity and hyperglycemia predispose patients to respiratory infections. Although the lung is a major organ to utilize glucose, pulmonary glucose homeostasis in type 2 diabetic (T2Dx) subjects remains poorly characterized. We hypothesized that pulmonary glucose transport would be altered during T2Dx, which would be rescued with long-term metformin treatment.

pmc-13178894.title: Feasibility and reliability of decentralized HIV-1 viral load monitoring on self-sampled blood
pmc-13178894.creator: Kyra F. Mendes de Leon, Suzanne Jurriaans, Roos D. Klungers, Janke Schinkel, Pythia T. Nieuwkerk, Marc van der Valk, Yury Khudyakov, Yury Khudyakov, Yury Khudyakov
pmc-13178894.description: BackgroundHome-based blood self-sampling for HIV-1 viral load (VL) monitoring has the potential to alleviate pressure on healthcare systems by reducing clinic visits for people with HIV. This study evaluates the feasibility and reliability of HIV-RNA measurements in self-sampled blood and in viremic samples.MethodsBetween September 2024 and March 2025 participants were recruited at the outpatient clinic.

pmc-13270635.title: Synthesis of Peptide-Oligonucleotide Conjugates via Condensation of a Lysine Side-Chain with a Thioester
pmc-13270635.creator: So Muramoto, Takashi Osawa, Satoshi Obika
pmc-13270635.description: Peptide-oligonucleotide conjugates (POCs) are promising drug delivery tools for oligonucleotide therapeutics. They are conventionally prepared by separately synthesizing peptides and oligonucleotides, introducing reactive functional groups into both molecules, and forming conjugates via click chemistry or maleimide-thiol coupling. However, these approaches generally require prefunctionalization of peptides or rely on the presence of cysteine residues, limiting their applicability to native peptides.

pmc-13320703.title: Universal-offer HIV testing amongst patients undergoing blood tests in primary care: results from a multi-centre study
pmc-13320703.creator: Rhys D Wenlock, Sean Perera, Jaime H Vera, Gillian Dean
pmc-13320703.description: BackgroundThe 2016 NICE guidelines recommend offering HIV testing alongside routine blood tests in areas of high HIV prevalence (>2 per 1000 adults aged 18–59). Despite this, implementation in primary care has been limited.MethodA universal-offer HIV testing intervention was implemented across seven general practices in Brighton and Hove.

pmc-13393671.title: Comparative analysis of genetic diversity and productive performance in Saudi native and carrier pigeon genotypes
pmc-13393671.creator: Sulaiman Aljumah, Ibrahim Al-Homidan, Mohamed Elzarei, Mohanad Ibrahim, Moataz Fathi
pmc-13393671.description: This study aimed to characterize the genetic diversity, population structure, and productive performance of three Saudi native pigeon populations (Spotted black-beak, SBB; White black-beak, WBB; White white-beak, WWB) in comparison with the Carrier genotype. Four genotypes were reared under identical management conditions. Carcass characteristics were evaluated based on genotype and sex.
